subject: Hospitality
title: Gleen Fogel: Booking.com's Rise
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Gleen Fogel: Booking.com's Rise.

hook.text: Booking Holdings—the parent of Booking.com—processes more hotel room nights than any company on Earth. Over 900 million per year.

buildup.text: Glenn Fogel became CEO in 2017 and pushed the 'connected trip' vision: flights, hotels, cars—all booked in one seamless flow.

discovery.text: Booking.com's commission model democratized hotel distribution. Any small guesthouse could list alongside Hilton on equal footing.

twist.text: Hotels resent paying 15–25% commissions but can't leave—Booking.com controls too much demand. Dependency breeds resentment.

climax.text: Fogel controls a distribution chokepoint. Whoever owns the search bar owns the customer.

punchline.text: 900 million room nights, 15–25% commission. The search bar is king.

quiz.question: How many room nights does Booking Holdings process annually?
